pr_title: [torch.compile] limit inductor threads and lazy import quant
pr_comments:
👋 Hi! Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.
 Just a reminder: PRs would not trigger full CI run by default. Instead, it would only run `fastcheck` CI which starts running only a small and essential subset of CI tests to quickly catch errors. You can run other CI tests on top of those by going to your `fastcheck` build on Buildkite UI (linked in the PR checks section) and unblock them. If you do not have permission to unblock, ping `simon-mo` or `khluu` to add you in our Buildkite org. 

Once the PR is approved and ready to go, your PR reviewer(s) can run CI to test the changes comprehensively before merging.

 To run CI, PR reviewers can do one of these:
- Add `ready` label to the PR
- Enable auto-merge.

🚀

the root cause is, quantization configs are imported too early. and when quantization configs are imported, `ParallelLMHead` is imported, triggering `@torch.compile` for `get_masked_input_and_mask` .

every process calling `torch.compile` will spawn many processes (cpu core number of processes), and having so many processes will cause vscode to hang.

### How would you like to use vllm


## Issue
After syncing to the latest main branch, I encountered a hanging issue while debugging vLLM code using VSCode. I found  that  many subprocess created by [torch.compile](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/vocab_parallel_embedding.py#L136), and the hanging occurs at [_run_in_subprocess](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py#L461). 

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25220b2f-a022-4046-8387-3c3dc1aaf886)


## Reproduce code
 Use [offline_inference.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/offline_inference.py)

## Temporary solution
- Set environment variable like:
```python
os.environ["TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS"]="1"
```
-  Configure VSCode: set subProcess: "false" in launch.json(Based on the feedback from Slack, I haven't actually tested it yet)

cc @youkaichao

comments: can you try if https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/10482 can help?

oh, for [_run_in_subprocess](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py#L461) , also cc @DarkLight1337  , it seems when we check the model in another process, it will trigger `torch.compile` .

review_comments: @DarkLight1337 this code already tests all registered quantization methods have the corresponding config, and the lazy import works.
Oh, I missed this, thanks for pointing it out!

The current approach does indeed solve my issue, and I've tested it locally without issues, thanks for your quick fixing. However, I'm concerned that in the future there might be import patterns similar to what we see with quantization now, which could cause torch.compile to initialize early again.
Do you see a compilation time hit from using just one thread @youkaichao ?
I measured it again, and compare it to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/10460 . I don't see any increase in compilation time. So this is a pure benefit.
@jeejeelee I added some tests to make sure it will not happen again.
